newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer on BOJ's generous stance.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer on BOJ's generous stance.

text.p: The key March Euroyen futures contract ended Thursday's session firmer as a recent accommodative credit stance by the Bank of Japan and falls in cash interest rates convinced the market the central bank will not change the key rate for at least a couple of months.
"The BOJ may raise the key rate as early as in October. But it's just too early to make positions for something that may or may not happen in the fall," said a city bank trader.
The key three-month certificate of deposit fell to as low as 0.67 percent on Thursday from the recent peak of 0.70 percent set on Tuesday.
The BOJ, through its aggressive liquidity injection into the money market, suggested a key CD rate of 0.70 percent had been too high under the current economic climate, traders said.
"The central bank's recent stance was telling the market that it's not going to move (on credit policy) in the near term," said a Japanese city bank trader.
The three-month cash Euroyen was traded at 0.74 percent, compared with the 0.74/0.76 percent quoted on Wednesday.
Since last Friday, the BOJ has let the market have massive surpluses to the tune of 300 billion to 400 billion yen, prompting rate falls across the spectrum in the money market.
A bullish JGB market as well as weak Tokyo stocks has also aided Euroyen futures' gains, traders said.

BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Thursday: "In managing our current monetary policy, it is appropriate to carefully watch developments (in the economy and prices), while continuing to put emphasis on strengthening the basis for economic recovery." Matsushita made the remark in a speech at a bankers' convention.

"We are observing a drop in demand due to the effects of the increase in the sales tax. But the recovery trend of the overall economy remains intact, with production and income holding firm," BOJ's Matsushita said.
Given steady improvements in employment and incomes, there is little chance that the recovery trend of private consumption in Japan will falter, Matsushita said.
Matsushita's remark underscored the bullish underlying tone in the Euroyen market, traders said.
